considerations.name: Kang, Temporal Tyrant
considerations.reason: 2nd-card payoff (each opp -1, +1) that connives itself — 2nd tier behind Gixian/Raven; UB not mono-B.

considerations.name: Starving Revenant
considerations.reason: Your-draw drain (opp -1, +1) but gated on Descend 8 — conditional.

considerations.name: Mind's Eye
considerations.reason: Draw when opponents draw (pay 1) — overlaps with what we run.

considerations.name: Sphinx's Tutelage
considerations.reason: Mills opponents on your draw — a slower alternate mill-kill, not drain.

considerations.name: Gollum, Riddle Master
considerations.reason: Hobbit: a mode is each opp -2 / you +2 (+ a draw mode), gated on opponent cast parity, fires each mode once.

considerations.name: Dawn of a New Age
considerations.reason: Hobbit: end-step draws (trigger Queza) then gain 4 (→ Exquisite drains 4) — slowish engine.

considerations.name: Reverent Howl
considerations.reason: Hobbit: 'target player draws two and loses 2' — drain an opponent AND feed Underworld/Bowmasters.

considerations.name: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth
considerations.reason: Win-more, 10 mana, off a low curve; reshuffle clogs the plan.

considerations.name: Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre
considerations.reason: 11 mana, no draw — nothing for a draw-drain deck.

considerations.name: Vexilus Praetor
considerations.reason: Protects Queza but advances the plan zero.

considerations.name: Campfire
considerations.reason: Dominated by Elixir (reshuffle without the lifegain rider).

considerations.name: Blue Sun's Zenith
considerations.reason: The controllable draw the research favored: draws you a bounded X and shuffles ITSELF back (never self-mills), or decks an opponent outright with big mana. Doubles as a 3rd wincon. Strongest of the reshuffle/valve options — promote if you want more redundancy.

considerations.name: Cliffhaven Vampire
considerations.reason: Redundant 'each opponent loses 1' gain→drain half ({2}{W}{B}, priciest and only-WB of the trio); Epicure + Marauding cover it cheaper in mono-B. Cut for Aetherflux Reservoir (an Exquisite Blood combo piece + cast-lifegain engine + 50-dmg finisher).

considerations.name: Soul Warden
considerations.reason: 1-life-per-creature-ETB igniter — low yield in a creature-light Esper deck; Venser's Journal is a far bigger repeatable lifegain source.

considerations.name: Children of Korlis
considerations.reason: One-shot situational regain (good after heavy life payment); cut for free permanent no-max (Spellbook).

considerations.name: Grim Monolith
considerations.reason: Interim ban-fix replacement, cut: makes COLORLESS mana (useless for this pip-hungry deck) and doesn't untap; deck already runs 11 rocks.
